hi.L: पर यदि तुम पक्षपात करते हो, तो पाप करते हो, और व्यवस्था के द्वारा उल्लंघन करनेवाले ठहराए जाते हो।
hi.B: पर यदि तुम पक्षपात करते हो, तो तुम पाप करते हो, और व्यवस्था तुम्हें व्यवस्था तोड़नेवाला ठहराती है।
hi.R: पर अगर तुम कुछ लोगों को दूसरों से ज़्यादा महत्व देते हो, तो तुम पाप कर रहे हो। व्यवस्था दिखाती है कि तुम उसे तोड़ने के दोषी हो।

ru.L: Если же вы оказываете лицеприятие, вы делаете грех, будучи обличаемы Законом как преступники.
ru.B: Но если вы оказываете предпочтение одним перед другими, вы совершаете грех, и Закон обличает вас как нарушителей.
ru.R: Но если вы ставите одних людей выше других, вы грешите. Закон показывает, что вы виновны в его нарушении.

uk.L: А якщо ви чините лицеприйняття, то робите гріх, викривані Законом як переступники.
uk.B: А якщо ви віддаєте перевагу одним людям перед іншими, то чините гріх, і Закон викриває вас як порушників.
uk.R: Але якщо ви ставите одних людей вище за інших, ви грішите. Закон показує, що ви винні в його порушенні.

ja.L: しかし、もし人をえこひいきするなら、あなたがたは罪を犯しているのであり、律法によって違反者として罪を指摘されています。
ja.B: しかし、人を分け隔てするなら、あなたがたは罪を犯すことになり、律法によって違反者と断定されます。
ja.R: しかし、人によって扱いを変えるなら、みなさんは罪を犯しているのです。律法は、みなさんが律法を破った者であることを示します。

decisions.choice: show favoritism: treat people by their status
decisions.reason: προσωπολημπτεῖτε is the verb from the noun in 2:1: to "lift the face" of someone, favoring the rich over the poor.

decisions.choice: convicted: exposed and proven guilty
decisions.reason: ἐλεγχόμενοι means to expose a wrong and prove it. The law itself is the witness against them, because it commands love of neighbor and forbids partiality (Leviticus 19:15, 18).

decisions.choice: transgressors: those who step over a set line
decisions.reason: παραβάτης is someone who breaks a definite command. Favoritism is not a small lapse in manners; it breaks God's law, and verses 10-11 explain why that makes them lawbreakers.

decisions.choice: convaincus ... comme transgresseurs (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means exposed and proven guilty (m2). French "convaincre" still has this legal sense ("convaincu de vol"), which Literal keeps; Balanced says what follows from it, "la Loi vous condamne".

source.text: ὅστις γὰρ ὅλον τὸν νόμον τηρήσῃ, πταίσῃ δὲ ἐν ἑνί, γέγονεν πάντων ἔνοχος.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever for whole the law keeps, stumbles but in one, has become of all guilty.

en.L: For whoever keeps the whole law but stumbles in one [point] has become guilty of all.
en.B: For if someone keeps the entire law and yet stumbles at one point, that person has become guilty of breaking all of it.
en.R: Suppose someone obeys the whole law except for one command. That person is guilty of breaking the whole law.

es.L: Porque cualquiera que guarde toda la ley, pero tropiece en un [punto], se ha hecho culpable de todos.
es.B: Porque si alguien guarda la ley entera, pero tropieza en un solo punto, se ha hecho culpable de quebrantarla toda.
es.R: Supongamos que alguien obedece toda la ley menos un mandamiento. Esa persona es culpable de quebrantar toda la ley.

sw.L: Kwa maana yeyote atakayeishika sheria yote, lakini akajikwaa katika [jambo] moja, amekuwa na hatia ya yote.
sw.B: Kwa maana mtu akiishika sheria yote, lakini akajikwaa katika jambo moja tu, amekuwa na hatia ya kuivunja yote.
sw.R: Tuseme mtu anaitii sheria yote isipokuwa amri moja. Mtu huyo ana hatia ya kuivunja sheria nzima.

fr.L: Car quiconque garde toute la Loi, mais trébuche sur un seul [point], est devenu coupable de tout.
fr.B: Car si quelqu’un observe la Loi tout entière mais trébuche sur un seul point, il est devenu coupable de l’avoir enfreinte tout entière.
fr.R: Imaginez quelqu’un qui obéit à toute la Loi, sauf à un seul commandement. Il est coupable d’avoir désobéi à toute la Loi.

ko.L: 누구든지 율법 전체를 지키다가 한 [조항]에서 걸려 넘어지면, 모든 것에 대해 죄가 있는 사람이 됩니다.
ko.B: 누구든지 율법 전체를 지키다가도 한 가지에서 걸려 넘어지면, 율법 전체를 어긴 죄가 있는 사람이 됩니다.
ko.R: 어떤 사람이 율법의 계명을 다 지키고 하나만 지키지 않았다고 해 봅시다. 그 사람은 율법 전체를 어긴 죄인입니다.

vi.L: Vì ai giữ trọn cả luật pháp mà vấp phạm một [điều], thì đã trở nên có tội với tất cả.
vi.B: Vì nếu ai giữ toàn bộ luật pháp mà chỉ vấp phạm một điều, thì người ấy đã mắc tội vi phạm tất cả.
vi.R: Giả sử có người vâng giữ cả luật pháp, chỉ trừ một điều răn. Người ấy vẫn có tội vì đã vi phạm cả luật pháp.

pt.L: Pois quem guardar toda a Lei, mas tropeçar em um [só ponto], tornou-se culpado de todos.
pt.B: Pois quem guarda a Lei inteira, mas tropeça num só ponto, torna-se culpado de quebrá-la toda.
pt.R: Imaginem alguém que obedece a toda a Lei, menos a um mandamento. Essa pessoa é culpada de quebrar a Lei inteira.

am.L: ሕጉን ሁሉ ጠብቆ በአንዱ [ትእዛዝ] የሚሰናከል ሁሉ የሁሉም በደለኛ ሆኗልና።
am.B: አንድ ሰው ሕጉን በሙሉ ጠብቆ በአንዲት ነጥብ ቢሰናከል፣ ሕጉን በሙሉ እንደ ጣሰ በደለኛ ሆኗልና።
am.R: አንድ ሰው ከአንዲት ትእዛዝ በቀር ሕጉን በሙሉ ይጠብቃል እንበል። ያ ሰው ሕጉን በሙሉ እንደ ጣሰ በደለኛ ነው።

hi.L: क्योंकि जो कोई पूरी व्यवस्था को माने, पर एक [बात] में ठोकर खाए, वह सब [बातों] का दोषी बन गया है।
hi.B: क्योंकि यदि कोई पूरी व्यवस्था का पालन करे और फिर भी एक बात में ठोकर खाए, तो वह सारी व्यवस्था तोड़ने का दोषी बन गया है।
hi.R: मान लो, कोई एक आज्ञा को छोड़कर बाक़ी सारी व्यवस्था मानता है। तब भी वह पूरी व्यवस्था तोड़ने का दोषी है।

ru.L: Ведь кто соблюдёт весь Закон, но споткнётся в одном, становится виновным во всём.
ru.B: Ведь если кто-то соблюдает весь Закон, но оступится в чём-то одном, он становится виновным в нарушении всего Закона.
ru.R: Допустим, кто-то исполняет весь Закон, кроме одной заповеди. Такой человек виновен в нарушении всего Закона.

uk.L: Бо хто виконає весь Закон, а спіткнеться в одному, той став винним у всьому.
uk.B: Бо коли хтось дотримується всього Закону, але спотикається в одному, той стає винним у порушенні всього Закону.
uk.R: Уявіть, що хтось виконує весь Закон, крім однієї заповіді. Така людина винна в порушенні всього Закону.

ja.L: なぜなら、だれでも律法全体を守っても、一つ[の点]でつまずくなら、すべてについて有罪となっているからです。
ja.B: 律法全体を守っていても、一つの点でつまずくなら、その人は律法全体を破った罪に問われることになるからです。
ja.R: ある人が、律法のおきてを一つだけ破り、ほかは全部守ったとしてみましょう。その人は、律法全体を破った罪のある人なのです。

decisions.choice: guilty of all: the law is one, because the one who gave it is one
alternatives: guilty of breaking every single command
decisions.reason: James does not mean that one sin is the same as committing every sin. The law is one whole, the expression of one Lawgiver's will (2:11; 4:12), so breaking any part of it makes a person a lawbreaker. ἔνοχος means liable, answerable before a court.

decisions.choice: a supposition: whoever should keep ... and stumble
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the subjunctive: James imagines a case to make his point. He does not suggest anyone keeps the whole law perfectly (3:2: all of us stumble in many things).

decisions.choice: guilty of breaking all of it; guilty of breaking the whole law
decisions.reason: "Guilty of all" is compressed in English. Balanced and Readable say what one is guilty of.

source.text: ὁ γὰρ εἰπών Μὴ μοιχεύσῃς εἶπεν καί Μὴ φονεύσῃς· εἰ δὲ οὐ μοιχεύεις φονεύεις δέ, γέγονας παραβάτης νόμου.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] for having said, Do not commit adultery, said also, Do not murder; if but not you commit adultery you murder but, you have become a transgressor of law.

en.L: For the one who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." Now if you do not commit adultery but you murder, you have become a transgressor of [the] law.
en.B: For the one who said, "Do not commit adultery," also said, "Do not murder." So if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have still broken the law.
en.R: God gave the command "Do not commit adultery," and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also gave the command "Do not murder." So if you never commit adultery but you murder someone, you are still a lawbreaker.

es.L: Porque el que dijo: «No cometas adulterio», dijo también: «No asesines». Ahora bien, si no cometes adulterio, pero asesinas, te has hecho transgresor de [la] ley.
es.B: Porque el que dijo: «No cometas adulterio», también dijo: «No asesines». Así que, si no cometes adulterio pero sí asesinas, igual has quebrantado la ley.
es.R: Dios dio el mandamiento «No cometas adulterio», y también dio el mandamiento «No asesines». Así que, si nunca cometes adulterio, pero asesinas a alguien, de todos modos has quebrantado la ley.

sw.L: Kwa maana yeye aliyesema, "Usizini," alisema pia, "Usiue." Basi, ikiwa huzini lakini unaua, umekuwa mvunjaji wa sheria.
sw.B: Kwa maana yule aliyesema, "Usizini," ndiye aliyesema pia, "Usiue." Kwa hiyo, ikiwa huzini lakini unaua, bado umeivunja sheria.
sw.R: Mungu alitoa amri, "Usizini," na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} pia alitoa amri, "Usiue." Kwa hiyo, kama hujawahi kuzini lakini umeua mtu, wewe bado ni mvunjaji wa sheria.

fr.L: Car celui qui a dit : « Ne commets pas d’adultère », a dit aussi : « Ne commets pas de meurtre. » Or si tu ne commets pas d’adultère mais que tu commets un meurtre, tu es devenu transgresseur de [la] Loi.
fr.B: Car celui qui a dit : « Ne commets pas d’adultère » a dit aussi : « Ne commets pas de meurtre. » Si donc tu ne commets pas d’adultère mais que tu commets un meurtre, tu as tout de même enfreint la Loi.
fr.R: Dieu a donné le commandement : « Ne commets pas d’adultère », et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a aussi donné le commandement : « Ne tue pas. » Alors, si tu ne commets jamais d’adultère mais que tu tues quelqu’un, tu as quand même désobéi à la Loi.

ko.L: "간음하지 마라" 하신 분이 "살인하지 마라"고도 하셨기 때문입니다. 그러므로 여러분이 간음하지 않더라도 살인하면, 율법을 범한 사람이 된 것입니다.
ko.B: "간음하지 마라" 하신 분이 "살인하지 마라"고도 하셨습니다. 그러니 여러분이 간음하지 않았더라도 살인했다면, 여러분은 율법을 어긴 것입니다.
ko.R: 하나님께서 "간음하지 마라" 하는 계명을 주셨고, "살인하지 마라" 하는 계명도 주셨습니다. 그러니 여러분이 간음은 하지 않았더라도 사람을 죽였다면, 여러분은 율법을 어긴 사람입니다.

vi.L: Vì Đấng đã phán: "Chớ phạm tội ngoại tình", cũng đã phán: "Chớ giết người." Vậy nếu anh chị em không phạm tội ngoại tình nhưng giết người, thì anh chị em đã trở nên kẻ vi phạm luật pháp.
vi.B: Vì Đấng đã phán: "Chớ phạm tội ngoại tình", cũng đã phán: "Chớ giết người." Vậy nếu anh chị em không ngoại tình nhưng lại giết người, thì anh chị em vẫn là người phạm luật.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã ban điều răn: "Đừng phạm tội ngoại tình", và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng ban điều răn: "Đừng giết người." Vậy nếu anh chị em không bao giờ ngoại tình nhưng lại giết người, thì anh chị em vẫn là người phạm luật.

pt.L: Pois aquele que disse: "Não adulterarás" também disse: "Não matarás." Ora, se você não adultera, mas mata, tornou-se transgressor da Lei.
pt.B: Pois quem disse "Não cometerás adultério" também disse "Não matarás". Assim, se você não comete adultério, mas mata, ainda assim quebrou a Lei.
pt.R: Deus deu o mandamento "Não cometas adultério", e {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} também deu o mandamento "Não mates". Então, se você nunca comete adultério, mas mata alguém, você continua sendo alguém que quebra a Lei.

am.L: «አታመንዝር» ያለው እርሱ ደግሞ «አትግደል» ብሏልና። ባታመነዝር ግን ብትገድል፣ ሕግ ተላላፊ ሆነሃል።
am.B: «አታመንዝር» ያለው እርሱ «አትግደል» ብሎም ተናግሯልና። ስለዚህ ባታመነዝር ነገር ግን ብትገድል፣ አሁንም ሕጉን ጥሰሃል።
am.R: እግዚአብሔር «አታመንዝር» የሚለውን ትእዛዝ ሰጥቷል፤ «ሰው አትግደል» የሚለውንም ትእዛዝ ሰጥቷል። ስለዚህ ፈጽሞ ባታመነዝር ግን ሰው ብትገድል፣ አሁንም ሕግ ተላላፊ ነህ።

hi.L: क्योंकि जिन्होंने कहा, "व्यभिचार न करना," उन्होंने यह भी कहा, "हत्या न करना।" अब यदि तुम व्यभिचार नहीं करते पर हत्या करते हो, तो तुम व्यवस्था का उल्लंघन करनेवाले बन गए हो।
hi.B: क्योंकि जिन्होंने कहा, "व्यभिचार मत करो," उन्होंने ही यह भी कहा, "हत्या मत करो।" इसलिए यदि तुम व्यभिचार नहीं करते पर हत्या करते हो, तो भी तुमने व्यवस्था तोड़ दी है।
hi.R: परमेश्वर ने आज्ञा दी, "व्यभिचार मत करो," और उन्होंने यह आज्ञा भी दी, "हत्या मत करो।" इसलिए अगर तुम कभी व्यभिचार नहीं करते पर किसी की हत्या करते हो, तो भी तुम व्यवस्था तोड़नेवाले हो।

ru.L: Ведь тот, кто сказал: «Не прелюбодействуй», сказал и: «Не убивай.» Если же ты не прелюбодействуешь, но убиваешь, ты стал преступником Закона.
ru.B: Ведь тот, кто сказал: «Не прелюбодействуй», сказал также: «Не убивай.» Так что если ты не прелюбодействуешь, но убиваешь, ты всё равно нарушил Закон.
ru.R: Бог дал заповедь «Не прелюбодействуй», и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} же дал заповедь «Не убивай.» Так что если ты никогда не изменяешь в браке, но убиваешь человека, ты всё равно нарушаешь Закон.

uk.L: Бо той, хто сказав: «Не чини перелюбу», сказав також: «Не вбивай.» А якщо ти не чиниш перелюбу, але вбиваєш, то став порушником Закону.
uk.B: Бо той, хто сказав: «Не чини перелюбу», сказав і: «Не вбивай.» Отже, якщо ти не чиниш перелюбу, але вбиваєш, ти все одно порушив Закон.
uk.R: Бог дав заповідь «Не чини перелюбу», і {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} же дав заповідь «Не вбивай». Тож якщо ти ніколи не чиниш перелюбу, але когось убиваєш, ти все одно порушник Закону.

ja.L: なぜなら、「姦淫してはならない」と言われた方は、「殺してはならない」とも言われたからです。そこで、もしあなたが姦淫しなくても、殺すなら、あなたは律法の違反者となっています。
ja.B: 「姦淫してはならない」と言われた方は、「殺してはならない」とも言われたからです。ですから、姦淫はしなくても人を殺せば、あなたは律法を破ったことになります。
ja.R: 神は「姦淫してはならない」というおきてを与え、「殺してはならない」というおきても与えられました。ですから、姦淫を一度もしたことがなくても、人を殺すなら、あなたは律法を破った者なのです。

decisions.choice: Do not commit adultery; Do not murder: the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: James quotes two of the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:13-14; Deuteronomy 5:17-18). He names adultery first, as Luke 18:20 and Romans 13:9 also do.

decisions.choice: the one who said: God, the one Lawgiver
decisions.reason: The commands have one source. Since the same God gave them all, obeying some and breaking others is still disobeying him (4:12 speaks of one lawgiver and judge).

decisions.choice: a transgressor of law: a lawbreaker, of the law as a whole
decisions.reason: νόμου has no article, which stresses what kind of person one becomes: a lawbreaker. The law in view is still the one law of verse 10.

decisions.choice: God gave the command
decisions.reason: Readable names God, the speaker the Greek refers to (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: y también dio el mandamiento
alternatives: y él también dio el mandamiento
decisions.reason: Spanish needs no subject pronoun here, so the English Readable's capitalisable "he" has no Spanish counterpart and there is no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: tu (singular) in the second half of the verse
decisions.reason: After the plural of verses 1-9, James turns to one reader with singular verbs, as in a debate. French can show this, so every level says "tu" here, where English "you" is the same for one or many.

decisions.choice: "간음하지 마라", "살인하지 마라", the commandments in the words of the Korean Matthew 19:18
decisions.reason: The Ten Commandments read as they do in the Korean Gospels, in the plain 해라체 of Scripture quoted. "-지 말라" is the written form used in the Korean Romans 13:9; the Gospels' "-지 마라" is kept here because it is the form of speech, and God is the speaker (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "phán" for God speaking the commandments
decisions.reason: The one who said is God, the one Lawgiver (m2). The Vietnamese style guide keeps "phán" for God speaking.

decisions.choice: você (James to one imagined reader); tu in the commandments
decisions.reason: James switches to the singular here and in 2:18-22, speaking to one imagined person, so Portuguese says "você" there and "vocês" elsewhere. The commandments keep God's "tu" ("Não matarás"; "Não mates" at R), as in Matthew 19:18 in Portuguese.

decisions.choice: honorific "जिन्होंने ... उन्होंने" for the one who said
decisions.reason: The speaker is God, the one Lawgiver (meaning decision m2), and God spoken of takes honorific forms (style guide, section 7b). So the honorific already shows who is meant where the English says "the one who".

decisions.choice: "व्यभिचार न करना", "हत्या न करना" (L); "... मत करो" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the commandments as Romans 13:9 has them. At Literal, Romans has the Greek future; here the Greek is a prohibition, so Literal says "न करना".

decisions.choice: «Не прелюбодействуй»; «Не убивай»
alternatives: Не будешь прелюбодействовать; не будешь убивать
decisions.reason: The Greek has the prohibitive subjunctive, not the future of Matthew 5:21 and Romans 13:9, so every level uses the imperative, as the Balanced of Matthew 5:27 does.

source.text: οὕτως λαλεῖτε καὶ οὕτως ποιεῖτε ὡς διὰ νόμου ἐλευθερίας μέλλοντες κρίνεσθαι.

records.literal_gloss: So speak and so do as by law of freedom being about to be judged.

en.L: So speak and so act as [those who are] about to be judged by [the] law of freedom.
en.B: Speak and act as people who are going to be judged by the law of freedom.
en.R: One day you will be judged by the law of freedom. So let that guide the way you speak and the way you act.

es.L: Así {{plural_you:hablen|hablad}} y así {{plural_you:actúen|actuad}}, como [quienes] van a ser juzgados por [la] ley de [la] libertad.
es.B: {{plural_you:Hablen|Hablad}} y {{plural_you:actúen|actuad}} como quienes van a ser juzgados por la ley de la libertad.
es.R: Un día {{plural_you:serán|seréis}} juzgados por la ley de la libertad. Por eso, {{plural_you:dejen|dejad}} que eso guíe {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} manera de hablar y {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} manera de actuar.

sw.L: Semeni hivyo na tendeni hivyo kama [watu] walio karibu kuhukumiwa kwa sheria ya uhuru.
sw.B: Semeni na kutenda kama watu watakaohukumiwa kwa sheria ya uhuru.
sw.R: Siku moja mtahukumiwa kwa sheria ya uhuru. Kwa hiyo, acheni jambo hilo liongoze jinsi mnavyosema na jinsi mnavyotenda.

fr.L: Parlez ainsi et agissez ainsi, comme [des gens] qui doivent être jugés par [la] loi de la liberté.
fr.B: Parlez et agissez comme des gens qui vont être jugés par la loi de la liberté.
fr.R: Un jour, vous serez jugés par la loi qui rend libre. Que cela guide donc votre manière de parler et votre manière d’agir.

ko.L: 여러분은 자유의 율법으로 심판을 받을 사람들답게 그렇게 말하고 그렇게 행하십시오.
ko.B: 자유를 주는 율법으로 심판을 받을 사람답게 말하고 행동하십시오.
ko.R: 언젠가 여러분은 자유를 주는 율법으로 심판을 받을 것입니다. 그러니 그것을 생각하며 말하고 행동하십시오.

vi.L: Hãy nói và hãy làm như [những người] sắp bị xét đoán bởi luật pháp của sự tự do.
vi.B: Hãy nói năng và hành động như những người sẽ bị xét xử theo luật pháp của sự tự do.
vi.R: Một ngày kia anh chị em sẽ bị xét xử theo luật pháp của sự tự do. Vậy hãy để điều đó dẫn dắt cách anh chị em nói và cách anh chị em làm.

pt.L: Assim falem e assim ajam, como [quem] está para ser julgado pela lei da liberdade.
pt.B: Falem e ajam como pessoas que vão ser julgadas pela lei da liberdade.
pt.R: Um dia vocês serão julgados pela lei da liberdade. Por isso, deixem que essa lei guie o modo como vocês falam e agem.

am.L: በነፃነት ሕግ ሊፈረድባችሁ እንዳላችሁ [ሰዎች] እንዲሁ ተናገሩ፤ እንዲሁም አድርጉ።
am.B: በነፃነት ሕግ ሊፈረድባቸው እንዳሉ ሰዎች ሆናችሁ ተናገሩ፤ አድርጉም።
am.R: አንድ ቀን በነፃነት ሕግ ይፈረድባችኋል። ስለዚህ ይህ እውነት በምትናገሩትና በምታደርጉት ነገር ሁሉ ይምራችሁ።

hi.L: तुम ऐसे बोलो और ऐसे करो, जैसे [वे लोग] जिनका स्वतंत्रता की व्यवस्था के द्वारा न्याय होनेवाला है।
hi.B: उन लोगों की तरह बोलो और काम करो जिनका न्याय स्वतंत्रता की व्यवस्था के द्वारा होनेवाला है।
hi.R: एक दिन स्वतंत्रता की व्यवस्था के द्वारा तुम्हारा न्याय होगा। इसलिए इसी बात को ध्यान में रखकर बोलो और काम करो।

ru.L: Так говорите и так поступайте, как те, кому предстоит быть судимыми по Закону свободы.
ru.B: Говорите и поступайте как люди, которых будут судить по Закону свободы.
ru.R: Однажды вас будут судить по Закону свободы. Пусть это определяет то, как вы говорите и как поступаете.

uk.L: Так говоріть і так чиніть, як ті, що мають бути суджені Законом свободи.
uk.B: Говоріть і дійте як люди, яких судитимуть за Законом свободи.
uk.R: Одного дня вас судитимуть за Законом свободи. Тож нехай це визначає, як ви говорите і як дієте.

ja.L: 自由の律法によって裁かれようとしている者として、そのように語り、そのように行いなさい。
ja.B: 自由の律法によって裁かれることになる者として、それにふさわしく語り、行いなさい。
ja.R: みなさんはいつか、人を自由にする律法によって裁かれます。ですから、そのことを心に留めて、話したり行動したりしてください。

decisions.choice: the law of freedom: God's law as it is given in the kingdom, the law that sets people free
alternatives: a law that gives permission to do as one likes
decisions.reason: James has called it "the perfect law of freedom" (1:25) and "the royal law" (2:8). It is God's law summed up in love of neighbor, which frees those who keep it rather than enslaving them (Psalm 119:45; John 8:31-32).

decisions.choice: as people about to be judged: the coming judgment is certain
decisions.reason: μέλλοντες with an infinitive speaks of what is sure to happen. The standard of judgment is the same law: God will look at how they spoke and acted toward others, including the poor.

decisions.choice: speak and act: words and deeds together
decisions.reason: James joins speaking and doing, as he joins hearing and doing (1:22). Their words to the rich and poor man (2:3) and their words to the hungry (2:16) will be judged along with their deeds.

decisions.choice: judgment first, then the command
decisions.reason: Readable states the fact first and then what follows from it, in two short sentences.

decisions.choice: "人を自由にする律法" (R); "自由の律法" (L, B)
decisions.reason: m1: the law that sets people free rather than enslaving them. Readable spells out what the genitive means, since "自由の律法" alone can read as a law about freedom.

source.text: ἡ γὰρ κρίσις ἀνέλεος τῷ μὴ ποιήσαντι ἔλεος· κατακαυχᾶται ἔλεος κρίσεως.

records.literal_gloss: The for judgment merciless to the [one] not having done mercy; boasts against mercy judgment.

en.L: For the judgment [will be] merciless to the one who has not shown mercy; mercy boasts against judgment.
en.B: Judgment will have no mercy on the one who has shown no mercy. Mercy wins out over judgment.
en.R: People who have not shown mercy will be judged without mercy. But mercy is stronger than judgment.

es.L: Porque el juicio [será] sin misericordia para el que no ha mostrado misericordia; la misericordia se jacta frente al juicio.
es.B: El juicio no tendrá misericordia de quien no ha tenido misericordia. La misericordia triunfa sobre el juicio.
es.R: Los que no han mostrado misericordia serán juzgados sin misericordia. Pero la misericordia es más fuerte que el juicio.

sw.L: Kwa maana hukumu [itakuwa] bila rehema kwa yule asiyeonyesha rehema; rehema inajisifu mbele ya hukumu.
sw.B: Hukumu haitakuwa na rehema kwa mtu asiyeonyesha rehema. Rehema hushinda hukumu.
sw.R: Watu ambao hawajaonyesha rehema watahukumiwa bila rehema. Lakini rehema ina nguvu kuliko hukumu.

fr.L: Car le jugement [sera] sans miséricorde pour celui qui n’a pas fait miséricorde ; la miséricorde se glorifie face au jugement.
fr.B: Le jugement sera sans miséricorde pour celui qui n’a pas fait preuve de miséricorde. La miséricorde l’emporte sur le jugement.
fr.R: Ceux qui n’ont pas été miséricordieux envers les autres seront jugés sans miséricorde. Mais la miséricorde est plus forte que le jugement.

ko.L: 긍휼을 베풀지 않은 사람에게는 긍휼 없는 심판이 [있을 것이기] 때문입니다. 긍휼은 심판을 이기고 자랑합니다.
ko.B: 긍휼을 베풀지 않은 사람은 긍휼 없는 심판을 받을 것입니다. 긍휼은 심판을 이깁니다.
ko.R: 다른 사람을 불쌍히 여기지 않은 사람은 하나님께서도 불쌍히 여기지 않고 심판하실 것입니다. 그러나 불쌍히 여기는 마음은 심판보다 강합니다.

vi.L: Vì sự xét đoán [sẽ] không có lòng thương xót đối với người không làm điều thương xót; lòng thương xót khoe mình trước sự xét đoán.
vi.B: Sự xét xử sẽ không thương xót người không có lòng thương xót. Lòng thương xót thắng hơn sự xét xử.
vi.R: Những người không tỏ lòng thương xót sẽ bị xét xử không chút thương xót. Nhưng lòng thương xót mạnh hơn sự xét xử.

pt.L: Pois o julgamento [será] sem misericórdia para quem não usou de misericórdia; a misericórdia se gloria contra o julgamento.
pt.B: O julgamento será sem misericórdia para quem não mostrou misericórdia. A misericórdia triunfa sobre o julgamento.
pt.R: Quem não teve misericórdia dos outros será julgado sem misericórdia. Mas a misericórdia é mais forte que o julgamento.

am.L: ምሕረት ላላደረገ ፍርዱ ምሕረት የሌለው ነውና፤ ምሕረት በፍርድ ላይ ይመካል።
am.B: ምሕረት ያላደረገ ሰው ያለ ምሕረት ይፈረድበታል። ምሕረት በፍርድ ላይ ያሸንፋል።
am.R: ለሌሎች ምሕረት ያላደረጉ ሰዎች ያለ ምሕረት ይፈረድባቸዋል። ምሕረት ግን ከፍርድ ይበረታል።

hi.L: क्योंकि जिसने दया नहीं की, उसका न्याय बिना दया के [होगा]; दया न्याय पर गर्व करती है।
hi.B: जिसने दया नहीं दिखाई, उसका न्याय भी बिना दया के होगा। दया न्याय पर जय पाती है।
hi.R: जिन लोगों ने दया नहीं दिखाई, उनका न्याय बिना दया के होगा। पर दया न्याय से ज़्यादा बलवान है।

ru.L: Ведь суд немилостив к не оказавшему милости; милость хвалится над судом.
ru.B: Суд не помилует того, кто сам не оказывал милости. Милость торжествует над судом.
ru.R: Люди, которые не были милосердны, будут судимы без милосердия. Но милосердие сильнее суда.

uk.L: Бо суд [буде] немилосердний до того, хто не чинив милосердя; милосердя хвалиться над судом.
uk.B: Суд не матиме милосердя до того, хто не виявив милосердя. Милосердя бере гору над судом.
uk.R: Людей, які не виявляли милосердя, судитимуть без милосердя. Але милосердя сильніше за суд.

ja.L: なぜなら、あわれみを行わなかった者には、あわれみのない裁きが[下る]からです。あわれみは裁きに対して誇ります。
ja.B: あわれみを示さなかった者は、あわれみのない裁きを受けます。あわれみは裁きに打ち勝つのです。
ja.R: ほかの人にあわれみを示さなかった人は、あわれみなしに裁かれます。けれども、あわれみは裁きよりも強いのです。

decisions.choice: judgment will be merciless: the future judgment of God
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb in the first clause. It continues verse 12, so the judgment is God's coming judgment. Jesus taught the same: "Blessed are the merciful, because mercy will be shown to them" (Matthew 5:7; 18:33-35).

decisions.choice: boasts against: triumphs over, stands unafraid before
decisions.reason: κατακαυχᾶται means to boast in triumph over someone. Mercy can face judgment without fear and win.

decisions.choice: mercy shown by people stands firm at the judgment
decisions.reason: The first clause speaks of those who show mercy or do not, so the mercy here is most likely the mercy a person has shown: it has nothing to fear at the judgment. Others take it as God's mercy, which is greater than his judgment. The two belong together, since those who show mercy are those who have received it (Matthew 18:33).

decisions.choice: wins out over; is stronger than
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the image of boasting. Balanced and Readable give its point, victory.

decisions.choice: se glorifie face au jugement (L)
decisions.reason: The verb is a compound of the one rendered "se glorifier" in 1:9 (m2): mercy stands before the judgment unafraid. Literal keeps the link; Balanced and Readable say that mercy wins.

decisions.choice: "긍휼" (L, B); "불쌍히 여기다" (R)
decisions.reason: "긍휼" is the established word for God's and people's mercy and is still understood; Readable uses the everyday "불쌍히 여기다". Readable names God as the judge, as the English Readable implies with "will be judged".

decisions.choice: "심판을 이기고 자랑합니다" (L); "심판을 이깁니다" (B); "심판보다 강합니다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is "boast against", used here for triumphing over judgment (meaning decision). Literal keeps "자랑하다" so the word can be traced; Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: "khoe mình trước" (L) for "boasts against"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb of boasting, "khoe mình" as in 1:9, so the reader sees that mercy stands unafraid before judgment (m2); Balanced and Readable say that it wins out, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ምሕረት (mercy), with "ምሕረት ያደረገ" for showing mercy
decisions.reason: James echoes Jesus' blessing on the merciful (Matthew 5:7), whose Amharic speaks of "መሐሪዎች" and "ምሕረት"; the same word is kept so the saying can be recognised. "ርኅራኄ" is kept for the Lord's compassion in 5:11.

source.text: Τί ὄφελος, ἀδελφοί μου, ἐὰν πίστιν λέγῃ τις ἔχειν ἔργα δὲ μὴ ἔχῃ;

records.literal_gloss: What [is] the profit, brothers of me, if faith says someone to have works but not he has?

en.L: What [is the] profit, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, if anyone says [he] has faith but has no works?
en.B: What use is it, my {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, for someone to claim faith if that person has no works?
en.R: My {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, what good is it if people say they have faith, but they have no actions to go with it?

es.L: ¿Qué provecho [hay], hermanos míos, si alguien dice tener fe, pero no tiene obras?
es.B: ¿De qué sirve, hermanos míos, que alguien afirme tener fe, si no tiene obras?
es.R: Hermanos míos, ¿de qué sirve que alguien diga que tiene fe, si no tiene obras que lo demuestren?

sw.L: Kuna faida gani, ndugu zangu, mtu akisema ana imani lakini hana matendo?
sw.B: Ndugu zangu, inafaa nini mtu kudai kuwa na imani ikiwa hana matendo?
sw.R: Ndugu zangu, ni faida gani watu wakisema wana imani, lakini hawana matendo yanayoendana nayo?

fr.L: Quel [est le] profit, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, si quelqu’un dit avoir la foi mais n’a pas d’œuvres ?
fr.B: À quoi cela sert-il, mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, que quelqu’un prétende avoir la foi s’il n’a pas d’œuvres ?
fr.R: Mes {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, à quoi cela sert-il de dire qu’on a la foi, si l’on n’a pas d’actes qui vont avec ?

ko.L: 내 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 누가 믿음이 있다고 말하면서 행함이 없다면, 무슨 유익이 [있겠습니까]?
ko.B: 내 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 어떤 사람이 믿음이 있다고 말하면서도 행함이 없다면, 그것이 무슨 소용이 있겠습니까?
ko.R: 내 {{gender:형제자매|형제}} 여러분, 어떤 사람이 믿음이 있다고 말하지만 그 믿음에 따르는 행동이 없다면, 그것이 무슨 쓸모가 있겠습니까?

vi.L: Có ích gì, thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, nếu ai nói mình có đức tin nhưng không có việc làm?
vi.B: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, nếu ai nói mình có đức tin mà không có việc làm, thì có ích gì?
vi.R: Thưa {{gender:anh chị em|anh em}} của tôi, nếu người ta nói mình có đức tin nhưng không có hành động đi kèm, thì có ích lợi gì?

pt.L: Que proveito [há], meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, se alguém diz ter fé, mas não tem obras?
pt.B: De que adianta, meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, alguém afirmar que tem fé, se não tem obras?
pt.R: Meus {{gender:irmãos e irmãs|irmãos}}, de que adianta as pessoas dizerem que têm fé, se não têm ações que combinem com essa fé?

am.L: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ ማንም እምነት አለኝ ቢል ሥራ ግን ባይኖረው ምን ይጠቅማል?
am.B: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ አንድ ሰው እምነት አለኝ ቢል፣ ነገር ግን ሥራ ከሌለው ምን ጥቅም አለው?
am.R: {{gender:ወንድሞቼና እኅቶቼ|ወንድሞቼ}} ሆይ፣ ሰዎች እምነት አለን ቢሉ፣ ነገር ግን እምነታቸውን የሚያሳይ ተግባር ባይኖራቸው ምን ይጠቅማል?

hi.L: क्या लाभ है, हे मेरे {{gender:भाइयो और बहनो|भाइयो}}, यदि कोई कहे कि उसके पास विश्वास है पर उसके पास काम न हों?
hi.B: मेरे {{gender:भाइयो और बहनो|भाइयो}}, यदि कोई दावा करे कि उसके पास विश्वास है, पर उसके पास काम न हों, तो इससे क्या लाभ?

ru.L: Какая польза, {{gender:братья и сёстры|братья}} мои, если кто говорит, что имеет веру, а дел не имеет?

decisions.choice: says he has faith: a claim to faith
decisions.reason: James does not say "if someone has faith" but "if someone says he has faith". The whole argument of 2:14-26 is about a faith that is only claimed, and verse 18 asks for it to be shown.

decisions.choice: works: the deeds that faith does, above all deeds of love and mercy
alternatives: works of the law, keeping the commands that set Jews apart, such as circumcision
decisions.reason: ἔργον here means what a person does. The examples are feeding and clothing a brother or sister (2:15-16), Abraham's offering of Isaac (2:21) and Rahab's sheltering of the messengers (2:25). They are not the "works of the law" that Paul says do not justify (Romans 3:28; Galatians 2:16).

decisions.choice: what profit: what good does it do
decisions.reason: ὄφελος is benefit, advantage. James asks what such faith does for the one who has it, and the next sentence answers: it cannot save. He asks the same question of empty words in 2:16.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: James is writing to the whole community of believers, women and men alike, so the inclusive form is the default; the traditional wording is the alternative.

decisions.choice: actions
decisions.reason: Readable says "actions" for ἔργον, a common word for what people do; Literal and Balanced keep "works" through 2:14-26 so that the argument's key word stays visible.

decisions.choice: obras at every level
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "actions" so that "works" is not heard as church jargon. Spanish "obras" is an everyday word for deeds, and keeping it at every level lets the reader follow James's one word through 2:14-26 and compare it with Paul's "obras de la ley".

decisions.choice: matendo at every level
decisions.reason: "Matendo" (deeds) is the settled word for works and is everyday Swahili, so it serves Readable too, where the English says "actions". It is the same word Romans uses for "matendo ya sheria", so James and Paul can be compared.

decisions.choice: les œuvres (L, B); les actes, ce qu’on fait (R) (for this chapter)
decisions.reason: "Les œuvres" is the established French word for the deeds faith does (m2), and Literal and Balanced keep it through 2:14-26 so the argument can be followed. Readable says "les actes" or "ce qu’on fait", as the English Readable says "actions".

decisions.choice: "행함" (L, B); "행동" (R) for works, through the chapter
alternatives: "행위", the word of the Korean Romans
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads works here as the deeds that faith does, above all deeds of love and mercy. "행함" (doing) links with "행하는 사람" (the doers of 1:22-25), as the Greek words link; Readable says "행동" (actions), as the English Readable does. The Korean Romans uses "행위" for the works of the law, and a reader comparing the two letters can see the different question each answers (meaning decision at 2:24).

decisions.choice: "đức tin" for faith and "việc làm" (L, B), "hành động" (R) for works, through 2:14-26
decisions.reason: "Đức tin" is the key term for faith in the Vietnamese Romans and Colossians. Works are the deeds faith does (m2): "việc làm" is the plain word, the one the reader will also meet in Paul; Readable says "hành động", as the English Readable says "actions".

decisions.choice: a fé; as obras (L, B); ações, o que faz (R)
decisions.reason: For 2:14-26: Literal and Balanced keep "obras" and "fé" throughout, the words of Romans 3-4 in Portuguese, so that the two passages can be compared; Readable says "ações", as the English Readable says "actions".

decisions.choice: ሥራ (works) at Literal and Balanced; ተግባር (deeds, action) at Readable, through the chapter
decisions.reason: "ሥራ" is the word Paul's letters use for works ("የሕግ ሥራ"), so a reader can set James 2 beside Romans 3-4; but it is also the everyday word for a job, so Readable says "ተግባር", what one actually does, as the English Readable says actions.

decisions.choice: "काम" at every level, never "कर्म"
decisions.reason: Romans settled "काम" for works, because "कर्म" carries the idea of karma. "काम" is also the everyday word for what people do, so Readable needs no other word where the English Readable says "actions", and the key word of 2:14-26 stays the same at every level, as in Romans 3-4.

decisions.choice: дела
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "actions"; Russian "дела" is already the everyday word for what people do, so it stays at every level through 2:14-26 and the key word of the argument can be followed, and compared with "дела Закона" in Romans.

decisions.choice: "діла" (L, B); "учинки" (R), through 2:14-26
decisions.reason: "Діла" is the Ukrainian word for works in the faith-and-works argument ("діла Закону" in Romans); Readable uses the everyday "учинки", as the English Readable says "actions".

decisions.choice: "行い" (L, B); "行動" (R), through 2:14-26
decisions.reason: As the English: Literal and Balanced keep one key word for the Greek word for works through the argument, and "行い" is the living word for it; Readable says "行動", what a person does, in line with the English Readable's "actions". "わざ" sounds churchly and old.

decisions.choice: the faith: that faith, the faith just described
decisions.reason: The article points back to the faith someone claims but does not show in works. James does not say faith cannot save; he says this kind cannot.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer no
decisions.reason: μὴ at the start of a question expects "no": such faith cannot save.

decisions.choice: save: rescue at God's final judgment
decisions.reason: James has just spoken of judgment (2:12-13) and uses the same verb of the word that is able to save souls (1:21; also 4:12; 5:20). The question is whether such faith will stand when God judges.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to "anyone" (2:14), man or woman. Literal keeps a pronoun, inclusive by default; Balanced and Readable say "the person" and "anyone", which need no setting.

decisions.choice: the generic masculine ("ሊያድነው", "ሰው") with no gender span, through the chapter
decisions.reason: In Amharic the masculine suffix used of "anyone" and the word "ሰው" (person) already include women, so a second option would read the same. Spans are kept for adelphos, "brother"; verse 15 names "a brother or a sister" in the Greek itself.

decisions.choice: "उसे" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Hindi "उसे" is not marked for gender, so there is nothing for the English setting on "them" or "him" to change (style guide, section 7). The same for the pronouns through this chapter.

decisions.choice: его (no gender span)
decisions.reason: The English Literal has a gender span on the pronoun for "anyone". Russian "кто" and its pronoun "он" already cover men and women, so there is no span on them in this chapter; it is kept for "brothers".

decisions.choice: "その人" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal has a gender span on the pronoun. Japanese "その人" already means a man or a woman, so no setting is needed.

source.text: ἐὰν ἀδελφὸς ἢ ἀδελφὴ γυμνοὶ ὑπάρχωσιν καὶ λειπόμενοι τῆς ἐφημέρου τροφῆς, εἴπῃ δέ τις αὐτοῖς ἐξ ὑμῶν· Ὑπάγετε ἐν εἰρήνῃ, θερμαίνεσθε καὶ χορτάζεσθε, μὴ δῶτε δὲ αὐτοῖς τὰ ἐπιτήδεια τοῦ σώματος, τί ὄφελος;

records.literal_gloss: If a brother or a sister naked are and lacking the daily food, \v 16 says and someone to them from you, Go in peace, be warmed and be filled, not you give but to them the necessities of the body, what [is] the profit?

en.L: If a brother or a sister is naked and lacking the food for the day, \v 16 and one of you says to them, "Go in peace, be warmed and be filled," but you do not give them the necessities of the body, what [is the] profit?
en.B: Suppose a brother or sister has no proper clothes and not enough food for the day, \v 16 and one of you tells them, "Go in peace; keep warm and eat well," but you do not give them what the body needs. What use is that?
en.R: Imagine a brother or sister who has nothing to wear and nothing to eat today. \v 16 One of you says to them, "Go in peace! Keep warm and eat all you want!" But none of you gives them anything their body needs. What good is that?

es.L: Si un hermano o una hermana están desnudos y les falta el alimento del día, \v 16 y alguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} les dice: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} en paz, {{plural_you:caliéntense|calentaos}} y {{plural_you:sáciense|saciaos}}», pero no les {{plural_you:dan|dais}} lo necesario para el cuerpo, ¿qué provecho [hay]?
es.B: Supongamos que un hermano o una hermana no tienen ropa suficiente ni comida para el día, \v 16 y uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} les dice: «{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} en paz; {{plural_you:abríguense|abrigaos}} y {{plural_you:coman|comed}} bien», pero no les {{plural_you:dan|dais}} lo que el cuerpo necesita. ¿De qué sirve eso?
es.R: {{plural_you:Imaginen|Imaginad}} a un hermano o una hermana que no tiene nada que ponerse ni nada que comer hoy. \v 16 Uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} les dice: «¡{{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} en paz! ¡{{plural_you:Abríguense|Abrigaos}} y {{plural_you:coman todo lo que quieran|comed todo lo que queráis}}!». Pero ninguno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} les da nada de lo que su cuerpo necesita. ¿De qué sirve eso?

sw.L: Ikiwa ndugu wa kiume au wa kike wako uchi na wanakosa chakula cha siku hiyo, \v 16 na mmoja wenu akawaambia, "Nendeni kwa amani, mpate joto na mshibe," lakini hamwapi mahitaji ya mwili, kuna faida gani?
sw.B: Tuseme ndugu wa kiume au wa kike hana nguo za kutosha wala chakula cha siku hiyo, \v 16 na mmoja wenu akawaambia, "Nendeni kwa amani; mpate joto na mle mshibe," lakini hamwapi mahitaji ya mwili. Inafaa nini?

fr.L: Si un frère ou une sœur sont nus et manquent de la nourriture du jour, \v 16 et que l’un de vous leur dise : « Allez en paix, chauffez-vous et rassasiez-vous », sans que vous leur donniez ce qui est nécessaire au corps, quel [en est le] profit ?
fr.B: Supposons qu’un frère ou une sœur n’ait pas de quoi se vêtir et manque de la nourriture de chaque jour, \v 16 et que l’un de vous leur dise : « Allez en paix ; tenez-vous au chaud et mangez à votre faim », mais que vous ne leur donniez pas ce dont le corps a besoin : à quoi cela sert-il ?
fr.R: Imaginez un frère ou une sœur qui n’a rien à se mettre et rien à manger aujourd’hui. \v 16 L’un de vous leur dit : « Allez en paix ! Restez au chaud et mangez autant que vous voulez ! » Mais personne parmi vous ne leur donne ce dont leur corps a besoin. À quoi cela sert-il ?

ko.L: 만일 형제나 자매가 헐벗고 그날 먹을 양식이 모자라는데, \v 16 여러분 가운데 누가 그들에게 "평안히 가십시오. 몸을 따뜻하게 하고 배불리 드십시오" 하고 말하면서도, 몸에 필요한 것들을 그들에게 주지 않는다면, 무슨 유익이 [있겠습니까]?
ko.B: 어떤 형제나 자매가 입을 옷도 변변치 않고 그날 먹을 양식도 없다고 합시다. \v 16 그런데 여러분 가운데 누가 그들에게 "평안히 가십시오. 따뜻하게 입고 배불리 드십시오" 하면서, 몸에 필요한 것은 주지 않는다면, 그것이 무슨 소용이 있겠습니까?
ko.R: 입을 것도 없고 오늘 먹을 것도 없는 형제나 자매가 있다고 생각해 보십시오. \v 16 여러분 가운데 누가 그들에게 "평안히 가십시오! 따뜻하게 지내고 많이 드십시오!" 하고 말합니다. 그러나 여러분 가운데 아무도 그들의 몸에 필요한 것을 주지 않습니다. 그것이 무슨 소용이 있습니까?

vi.L: Nếu một anh em hoặc một chị em không có áo mặc và thiếu lương thực hằng ngày, \v 16 mà một người trong anh chị em nói với họ: "Hãy đi bình an, hãy sưởi ấm và ăn no", nhưng anh chị em không cho họ những thứ cần thiết cho thân thể, thì có ích gì?
vi.B: Giả sử có một anh em hay chị em không đủ áo mặc và thiếu cái ăn hằng ngày, \v 16 mà một người trong anh chị em bảo họ: "Hãy đi bình an, giữ cho ấm và ăn uống no đủ nhé", nhưng anh chị em lại không cho họ những gì thân thể cần, thì có ích gì?
vi.R: Hãy hình dung có một anh em hay chị em không có gì để mặc và hôm nay không có gì để ăn. \v 16 Một người trong anh chị em nói với họ: "Chúc đi bình an! Giữ cho ấm và ăn cho no nhé!" Nhưng không ai trong anh chị em cho họ những gì thân thể họ cần. Như vậy thì có ích lợi gì?

pt.L: Se um irmão ou uma irmã estiverem nus e lhes faltar o alimento de cada dia, \v 16 e algum de vocês lhes disser: "Vão em paz, aqueçam-se e fartem-se", mas vocês não lhes derem o necessário para o corpo, que proveito [há]?
pt.B: Suponham que um irmão ou uma irmã não tenha roupa adequada nem comida suficiente para o dia, \v 16 e que um de vocês lhes diga: "Vão em paz; agasalhem-se e comam bem", mas vocês não lhes deem aquilo de que o corpo precisa. De que adianta isso?
pt.R: Imaginem um irmão ou uma irmã que não tem o que vestir nem o que comer hoje. \v 16 Um de vocês diz a eles: "Vão em paz! Fiquem bem agasalhados e comam até ficar satisfeitos!" Mas nenhum de vocês dá a eles nada daquilo de que o corpo precisa. De que adianta isso?

am.L: ወንድም ወይም እኅት ተራቁተው የዕለት ምግብም ቢያጡ፣ \v 16 ከእናንተም አንዱ «በሰላም ሂዱ፤ ሙቁ፤ ጥገቡም» ቢላቸው፣ ለሰውነት የሚያስፈልገውን ግን ባትሰጧቸው፣ ምን ይጠቅማል?
am.B: አንድ ወንድም ወይም እኅት የሚለብሱት ልብስ ቢያጡና የዕለት ምግብ ቢጎድላቸው፣ \v 16 ከእናንተም አንዱ «በሰላም ሂዱ፤ ይሙቃችሁ፤ በደንብም ብሉ» ቢላቸው፣ ነገር ግን ለሰውነታቸው የሚያስፈልገውን ባትሰጧቸው፣ ይህ ምን ይጠቅማል?

ru.L: Если брат или сестра наги и лишены дневного пропитания, \v 16 а кто-нибудь из вас скажет им: «Идите с миром, грейтесь и насыщайтесь», но не дадите им необходимого для тела, — какая польза?
ru.B: Допустим, у брата или сестры нет нормальной одежды и не хватает еды на день, \v 16 и кто-то из вас говорит им: «Идите с миром, грейтесь и ешьте досыта», а вы не даёте им того, что нужно для тела. Какая от этого польза?

uk.L: Якщо брат або сестра голі й не мають їжі на день, \v 16 а хтось із вас скаже їм: «Ідіть з миром, грійтеся і насичуйтеся», але ви не дасте їм потрібного для тіла, — яка користь?

uk.R: Уявіть брата чи сестру, яким нема чого вдягнути і нема що їсти сьогодні. \v 16 Хтось із вас каже їм: «Ідіть з миром! Грійтеся і їжте досхочу!» Але ніхто з вас не дає їм нічого, чого потребує їхнє тіло. Яка з цього користь?

ja.L: もし兄弟か姉妹が裸で、その日の食べ物にも欠いているとき、\v 16 あなたがたのうちのだれかがその人たちに、「平安のうちに行きなさい。温まり、満腹になりなさい」と言うのに、あなたがたが体に必要なものをその人たちに与えないなら、何の益が[ありますか]？

decisions.choice: naked: without proper clothing
decisions.reason: γυμνοὶ can mean wearing only an undergarment, without the outer cloak that kept a person warm at night (Exodus 22:26-27; John 21:7). Hence "keep warm" in verse 16.

decisions.choice: the food for the day: what is needed to eat today
decisions.reason: ἐφημέρου means "for the day". They do not have even today's food, which is what Jesus taught his followers to pray for (Matthew 6:11).

decisions.choice: Go in peace: a customary farewell
decisions.reason: "Go in peace" was an everyday blessing at parting (Judges 18:6; 1 Samuel 1:17; Mark 5:34). Here it is a kind word used to send needy people away empty-handed.

decisions.choice: one of you says, but you do not give: the whole church shares the blame
decisions.reason: "One of you" speaks, but the verb "give" is plural: none of them helps. The community that lets the words stand without the help is responsible together.

decisions.choice: a brother or sister
decisions.reason: The Greek names both, so English does too; no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: keep warm and eat well; Keep warm and eat all you want
decisions.reason: The verbs can be middle ("warm yourselves") or passive ("be warmed"); either way they are wishes with no help behind them. Balanced and Readable give them as the casual well-wishing they are.

decisions.choice: plural_you on the farewell to the brother and sister
decisions.reason: The farewell is spoken to two people, not to James's readers, but a reader who has chosen vosotros would find "Vayan en paz" foreign, so the commands follow the same setting ("Vayan" | "Id").

decisions.choice: ndugu wa kiume au wa kike
decisions.reason: Swahili "ndugu" covers both ἀδελφὸς and ἀδελφὴ, so "wa kiume" and "wa kike" are added to keep James's two words apart. "Dada" would also work but is more often a sister by birth.

decisions.choice: "형제나 자매" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Greek names both, a brother or a sister, so Korean says both in every setting, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "평안히 가십시오" for the farewell
decisions.reason: "Go in peace" was a customary farewell (meaning decision); Korean "평안히 가십시오" is natural and keeps the word "peace", which the hollow wish makes ironic.

decisions.choice: "một anh em hoặc một chị em", with no gender span
decisions.reason: James names both a brother and a sister, so Vietnamese names both plainly; there is no traditional wording for a setting to offer.

decisions.choice: "平安のうちに行きなさい" (L, B); "安心して行きなさい" (R)
decisions.reason: m3: a customary farewell blessing. Literal and Balanced keep the blessing with "平安", the word for peace as a greeting; Readable uses the everyday phrase. The plain register of the speech fits a believer sending a brother or sister away.

decisions.choice: the speaker's words are only "You have faith, and I have works", as the SBLGNT punctuates
alternatives: the quotation runs on to the end of verse 18 or 19
the speaker is on James's side
decisions.reason: The Greek has no quotation marks, and where this speaker stops is one of the hardest questions in the letter. The SBLGNT ends the quotation after "I have works", so the next sentence is James's reply. This record follows it.

decisions.choice: "you" and "I" mean "one person" and "another": faith and works are separate gifts
alternatives: the speaker is an ally who has works, speaking to the one who has only faith
decisions.reason: Read with the SBLGNT's punctuation, the objector seems to say that faith and works can be found in different people, so that one may have the first without the second. James answers that faith cannot be shown without works. Others hear an ally supporting James, but "But someone will say" usually introduces an objection (1 Corinthians 15:35; Romans 9:19).

decisions.choice: One person has faith, and another has actions
alternatives: You have faith, and I have works
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the meaning chosen in the meaning decision: "you" and "I" stand for any two people.

decisions.choice: actions
decisions.reason: Readable says "actions" for ἔργον, a common word for what people do; Literal and Balanced keep "works" through 2:14-26 so that the argument's key word stays visible.

decisions.choice: "당신" with 합쇼체 for the singular "you" of the imagined objector and of James's answer, through verse 22
decisions.reason: James argues with an imagined speaker in the singular. As in the Korean of Romans 2:1 and 8:2, the letter's 합쇼체 is kept and "당신" gives the singular "you" of a debate; the plain 해라체 would sound like contempt.

decisions.choice: "Bạn ... tôi" (L, B) in the objector's words, and "bạn" for the singular "you" in 2:18-22
decisions.reason: James argues with an imagined hearer, as Paul does in Romans; Vietnamese gives that hearer the neutral "bạn", as the Vietnamese Romans does. Readable says what the "you" and "I" stand for, one person and another (m2), as the English Readable does.

sw.B: Nionyeshe imani yako isiyo na matendo yoyote, nami nitakudhihirishia imani yangu kupitia matendo yangu.
sw.R: Nionyeshe imani yako kama huna matendo! Mimi nitakuonyesha imani yangu kwa yale ninayotenda.

fr.L: Montre-moi ta foi sans les œuvres, et moi, je te montrerai, par mes œuvres, [ma] foi.
fr.B: Montre-moi ta foi sans aucune œuvre, et moi, c’est par mes œuvres que je te montrerai ma foi.
fr.R: Montre-moi ta foi, si tu n’as pas d’actes ! Moi, je te montrerai ma foi par ce que je fais.

ko.L: 행함이 없는 당신의 믿음을 내게 보여 주십시오. 그러면 나는 내 행함으로 [내] 믿음을 당신에게 보여 주겠습니다.
ko.B: 행함이 없는 당신의 믿음을 내게 보여 주십시오. 나는 내 행함으로 내 믿음을 당신에게 보여 주겠습니다.
ko.R: 행동이 없는데 믿음이 있다면, 그 믿음을 나에게 보여 주십시오! 나는 내가 하는 일로 내 믿음을 당신에게 보여 주겠습니다.

vi.L: Hãy chỉ cho tôi thấy đức tin của bạn không có việc làm, còn tôi, bởi việc làm của tôi, sẽ chỉ cho bạn thấy đức tin [của tôi].
vi.B: Hãy chỉ cho tôi thấy đức tin của bạn mà không có việc làm nào, còn tôi sẽ chỉ cho bạn thấy đức tin của tôi qua việc làm của tôi.
vi.R: Nếu bạn không có hành động, hãy thử chỉ cho tôi thấy đức tin của bạn! Còn tôi sẽ chỉ cho bạn thấy đức tin của tôi qua những gì tôi làm.

pt.L: Mostre-me a sua fé sem as obras, e eu lhe mostrarei, pelas minhas obras, a [minha] fé.
pt.B: Mostre-me a sua fé sem obras, e eu lhe mostrarei a minha fé por meio das minhas obras.
pt.R: Mostre-me a sua fé, se você não tem ações! Eu vou mostrar a você a minha fé pelo que eu faço.

am.L: እምነትህን ያለ ሥራ አሳየኝ፤ እኔም ከሥራዬ እምነቴን አሳይሃለሁ።
am.B: እምነትህን ያለ ምንም ሥራ አሳየኝ፤ እኔ ደግሞ እምነቴን በሥራዬ አሳይሃለሁ።
am.R: ተግባር ሳይኖርህ እምነትህን እስቲ አሳየኝ! እኔ ግን እምነቴን በማደርገው ነገር አሳይሃለሁ።

hi.L: तुम मुझे अपना विश्वास कामों के बिना दिखाओ, और मैं तुम्हें अपने कामों के द्वारा [अपना] विश्वास दिखाऊँगा।
hi.B: बिना किसी काम के अपना विश्वास मुझे दिखाओ, और मैं अपने कामों के द्वारा तुम्हें अपना विश्वास दिखाऊँगा।
hi.R: अगर तुम्हारे पास कोई काम नहीं हैं, तो अपना विश्वास मुझे दिखाकर देखो! मैं तो जो करता हूँ, उसी से तुम्हें अपना विश्वास दिखाऊँगा।

ru.L: Покажи мне твою веру без дел, а я покажу тебе из моих дел [мою] веру.
ru.B: Покажи мне свою веру без всяких дел, а я покажу тебе свою веру через мои дела.
ru.R: Попробуй показать мне свою веру, если у тебя нет дел! А я покажу тебе свою веру тем, что я делаю.

uk.L: Покажи мені свою віру без діл, а я тобі покажу з моїх діл [мою] віру.
uk.B: Покажи мені свою віру без жодних діл, а я покажу тобі свою віру через мої діла.
uk.R: Покажи мені свою віру, якщо в тебе немає вчинків! А я покажу тобі свою віру тим, що роблю.

ja.L: 行いなしに、あなたの信仰をわたしに見せなさい。そうすれば、わたしは行いによって、[わたしの]信仰をあなたに見せましょう。
ja.B: 行いのないあなたの信仰を、わたしに見せてみなさい。わたしは、行いによって自分の信仰をあなたに見せましょう。
ja.R: 行動がないのに信仰があると言うなら、その信仰をわたしに見せてください！わたしは、自分のしていることで、わたしの信仰を見せましょう。

decisions.choice: show me your faith without works: a challenge that cannot be met
decisions.reason: δεῖξόν is an imperative, but James means it as a challenge: faith cannot be seen apart from what it does. The point is not that works replace faith but that works are how faith is seen.

decisions.choice: by my works ... my faith: faith made visible through what it does
decisions.reason: James does not set his works against his faith. He will show the faith itself, by means of the works that come from it, as Abraham's faith was seen in what he did (2:22).

decisions.choice: by what I do
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the plain verb here; "actions" stands earlier in the sentence.

source.text: σὺ πιστεύεις ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν ὁ θεός;

records.literal_gloss: You believe that one is the God?

en.L: You believe that God is one?
en.B: You believe that God is one?
en.R: Do you believe that God is one, that there is only one God?

es.L: ¿Tú crees que Dios es uno?
es.B: ¿Tú crees que Dios es uno?
es.R: ¿Crees que Dios es uno, que solo hay un Dios?

sw.L: Wewe unaamini kwamba Mungu ni mmoja?
sw.B: Je, unaamini kwamba Mungu ni mmoja?
sw.R: Je, unaamini kwamba Mungu ni mmoja, kwamba kuna Mungu mmoja tu?

fr.L: Toi, tu crois que Dieu est un ?
fr.B: Tu crois que Dieu est un ?
fr.R: Crois-tu que Dieu est un, qu’il n’y a qu’un seul Dieu ?

ko.L: 당신은 하나님께서 한 분이시라는 것을 믿습니까?
ko.B: 당신은 하나님께서 한 분이시라는 것을 믿습니까?
ko.R: 당신은 하나님께서 한 분이시라는 것, 곧 하나님은 오직 한 분뿐이시라는 것을 믿습니까?

vi.L: Bạn tin rằng Đức Chúa Trời là một ư?
vi.B: Bạn tin rằng Đức Chúa Trời là một ư?
vi.R: Bạn có tin rằng Đức Chúa Trời là một, rằng chỉ có một Đức Chúa Trời không?

pt.L: Você crê que Deus é um?
pt.B: Você crê que Deus é um só?
pt.R: Você crê que Deus é um só, que existe apenas um Deus?

am.L: አንተ እግዚአብሔር አንድ እንደ ሆነ ታምናለህ?
am.B: አንተ እግዚአብሔር አንድ እንደ ሆነ ታምናለህ?
am.R: እግዚአብሔር አንድ እንደ ሆነ፣ ከእርሱ በቀር ሌላ አምላክ እንደሌለ ታምናለህ?

hi.L: तुम विश्वास करते हो कि परमेश्वर एक है?
hi.B: क्या तुम विश्वास करते हो कि परमेश्वर एक है?
hi.R: क्या तुम विश्वास करते हो कि परमेश्वर एक है, कि केवल एक ही परमेश्वर है?

ru.L: Ты веришь, что Бог один?
ru.B: Ты веришь, что Бог один?
ru.R: Ты веришь, что Бог один, что есть только один Бог?

uk.L: Ти віриш, що Бог один?
uk.B: Ти віриш, що Бог один?
uk.R: Ти віриш, що Бог один, що є тільки один Бог?

ja.L: あなたは、神はひとりであると信じていますか？
ja.B: あなたは、神はただひとりであると信じているのですか？
ja.R: あなたは、神がひとりであること、つまり、神はただひとりの方しかおられないことを信じていますか？

decisions.choice: God is one: the Shema, Deuteronomy 6:4
decisions.reason: "Hear, Israel: the LORD is our God; the LORD is one" (Deuteronomy 6:4). It was the central confession of Israel's faith, recited daily, and Jesus called it the first command (Mark 12:29). James's readers would all have confessed it.

decisions.choice: a question, as the SBLGNT punctuates
alternatives: a statement: "You believe that God is one."
decisions.reason: The Greek words can be read as a statement or as a question; the SBLGNT has a question mark. The meaning is the same: the reader holds the right belief.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "God is one"
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ in the order of these words and in whether "God" has the article, and some can be read as "there is one God". The confession is the same in all of them. From general knowledge; reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: that there is only one God
decisions.reason: Readable adds what the confession means, so a new reader does not take "one" as a number to count.

source.text: καλῶς ποιεῖς· καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια πιστεύουσιν καὶ φρίσσουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Well you do; also the demons believe and shudder.

en.L: You do well; the demons also believe, and they shudder.
en.B: Well and good! The demons believe it too, and they tremble.
en.R: That is good! But the demons believe that as well, and they shake with fear.

es.L: Haces bien; también los demonios creen, y se estremecen.
es.B: ¡Muy bien! También los demonios lo creen, y tiemblan.
es.R: ¡Eso está bien! Pero los demonios también lo creen, y tiemblan de miedo.

sw.L: Unafanya vizuri; pepo nao wanaamini, na wanatetemeka.
sw.B: Vema sana! Pepo pia wanaamini hivyo, nao wanatetemeka.
sw.R: Hilo ni jema! Lakini hata pepo wanaamini hivyo, nao wanatetemeka kwa hofu.

fr.L: Tu fais bien ; les démons aussi croient, et ils frissonnent.
fr.B: C’est très bien ! Les démons aussi le croient, et ils tremblent.
fr.R: C’est bien ! Mais les démons le croient aussi, et ils tremblent de peur.

ko.L: 잘하는 것입니다. 귀신들도 믿고 떱니다.
ko.B: 잘하는 일입니다! 귀신들도 그것을 믿고 떱니다.
ko.R: 좋습니다! 그러나 귀신들도 그것을 믿고, 두려워서 벌벌 떱니다.

vi.L: Bạn làm phải lắm; các quỷ cũng tin, và chúng run sợ.
vi.B: Tốt lắm! Các quỷ cũng tin như vậy, và chúng run rẩy.
vi.R: Điều đó tốt! Nhưng các quỷ cũng tin như thế, và chúng run lên vì sợ hãi.

pt.L: Faz bem; também os demônios creem, e estremecem.
pt.B: Muito bem! Os demônios também creem nisso, e tremem.
pt.R: Isso é bom! Mas os demônios também acreditam nisso, e tremem de medo.

am.L: መልካም ታደርጋለህ፤ አጋንንትም ደግሞ ያምናሉ፤ ይንቀጠቀጣሉም።
am.B: መልካም ነው! አጋንንትም ያምናሉ፤ ይንቀጠቀጣሉም።
am.R: ይህ ጥሩ ነው! ነገር ግን አጋንንትም ይህን ያምናሉ፤ በፍርሃትም ይንቀጠቀጣሉ።

hi.L: तुम अच्छा करते हो; दुष्टात्माएँ भी विश्वास करती हैं और काँपती हैं।
hi.B: बहुत अच्छा! दुष्टात्माएँ भी यह विश्वास करती हैं, और थरथराती हैं।
hi.R: यह अच्छी बात है! पर दुष्टात्माएँ भी यह विश्वास करती हैं, और डर के मारे काँपती हैं।

ru.L: Хорошо делаешь; и бесы верят и трепещут.
ru.B: Хорошо! Бесы тоже в это верят и дрожат.
ru.R: Это хорошо! Но и бесы верят в это и дрожат от страха.

uk.L: Добре робиш; і біси вірять і тремтять.
uk.B: Добре! Біси теж у це вірять — і тремтять.
uk.R: Це добре! Але й біси в це вірять, і вони тремтять від страху.

ja.L: あなたは良いことをしています。悪霊たちもまた信じて、身震いしています。
ja.B: それは結構なことです。悪霊たちもそれを信じて、おののいています。
ja.R: それはよいことです。けれども、悪霊たちも同じことを信じていて、怖くて震えているのです。

decisions.choice: you do well: real approval, with an edge
decisions.reason: καλῶς ποιεῖς approves of the belief: it is true. But in the next breath James shows that agreeing with a true statement is not the faith he means. It is the same phrase as in 2:8.

decisions.choice: believe: hold to be true, without trust or obedience
decisions.reason: The demons believe the same thing: they know who God is (Mark 1:24; 5:7). Belief that only agrees with the facts is not the faith that saves.

decisions.choice: shudder: tremble with terror
decisions.reason: φρίσσουσιν means to bristle or shudder with fear. The demons' belief brings no peace, only dread of the God they know will judge them.

decisions.choice: "귀신들" for the demons
decisions.reason: "마귀" is the word for the devil (4:7), so the demons are "귀신", as in the Korean of the Gospels.

decisions.choice: "các quỷ" and "chúng" for the demons; "ma quỷ" is kept for the devil (4:7)
decisions.reason: The demons are evil spirits, and Vietnamese gives them the pronoun "chúng", used for beings one stands against. "Ma quỷ" names the devil in the style guide, so the two are kept apart.

source.text: θέλεις δὲ γνῶναι, ὦ ἄνθρωπε κενέ, ὅτι ἡ πίστις χωρὶς τῶν ἔργων ἀργή ἐστιν;

records.literal_gloss: Want you and to know, O man empty, that the faith without the works useless is?

en.L: And do you want to know, O empty {{gender:person|man}}, that faith without the works is useless?
en.B: Do you want to be shown, you empty-headed {{gender:person|man}}, that faith without works does no work?
en.R: You foolish {{gender:person|man}}! Do you want me to show you that faith without actions is good for nothing?

es.L: ¿Y quieres saber, oh {{gender:persona vacía|hombre vacío}}, que la fe sin las obras es inútil?
es.B: ¿Quieres que te demuestre, {{gender:persona insensata|hombre insensato}}, que la fe sin obras no obra?
es.R: ¡{{gender:Persona necia|Hombre necio}}! ¿Quieres que te muestre que la fe sin obras no sirve para nada?

sw.L: Na unataka kujua, ewe mtu mtupu, kwamba imani bila matendo ni ya bure?
sw.B: Je, unataka kuonyeshwa, ewe mtu usiye na akili, kwamba imani isiyo na matendo haitendi chochote?
sw.R: Ewe mtu mpumbavu! Unataka nikuonyeshe kwamba imani isiyo na matendo haifai kitu?

fr.L: Mais veux-tu savoir, ô {{gender:personne vide|homme vide}}, que la foi sans les œuvres est inutile ?
fr.B: Veux-tu donc qu’on te montre, {{gender:tête vide|homme vide}}, que la foi sans les œuvres ne produit rien ?
fr.R: {{gender:Personne insensée|Homme insensé}} ! Veux-tu que je te montre que la foi sans actes ne sert à rien ?

ko.L: 그런데 오, 허망한 사람이여, 행함이 없는 믿음이 쓸모없다는 것을 알고 싶습니까?
ko.B: 생각이 텅 빈 사람이여, 행함이 없는 믿음은 아무 일도 하지 못한다는 것을 보여 줄까요?
ko.R: 어리석은 사람이여! 행동이 없는 믿음은 아무짝에도 쓸모없다는 것을 내가 보여 줄까요?

vi.L: Nhưng hỡi người rỗng tuếch kia, bạn có muốn biết rằng đức tin không có việc làm là vô dụng không?
vi.B: Hỡi người rỗng tuếch kia, bạn có muốn được chỉ cho thấy rằng đức tin không có việc làm thì chẳng làm được việc gì không?
vi.R: Bạn thật dại dột! Bạn có muốn tôi chỉ cho bạn thấy rằng đức tin không có hành động thì chẳng được tích sự gì không?

pt.L: Mas você quer saber, ó {{gender:pessoa vazia|homem vazio}}, que a fé sem as obras é inútil?
pt.B: Você quer que eu lhe mostre, {{gender:pessoa sem juízo|homem sem juízo}}, que a fé sem obras não faz obra nenhuma?
pt.R: {{gender:Pessoa tola|Homem tolo}}! Você quer que eu mostre a você que a fé sem ações não serve para nada?

am.L: አንተ ባዶ ሰው ሆይ፣ እምነት ያለ ሥራ ሥራ ፈት እንደ ሆነ ልታውቅ ትወዳለህን?
am.B: አንተ ከንቱ ሰው፣ ሥራ የሌለው እምነት ሥራ ፈት እንደ ሆነ ልታይ ትፈልጋለህን?
am.R: አንተ ሞኝ ሰው! ተግባር የሌለው እምነት ለምንም እንደማይጠቅም ላሳይህ ትፈልጋለህ?

hi.L: और हे खोखले मनुष्य, क्या तुम जानना चाहते हो कि कामों के बिना विश्वास बेकार है?
hi.B: हे नासमझ मनुष्य, क्या तुम चाहते हो कि तुम्हें दिखाया जाए कि कामों के बिना विश्वास कोई काम नहीं करता?
hi.R: हे मूर्ख मनुष्य! क्या तुम चाहते हो कि मैं तुम्हें दिखाऊँ कि कामों के बिना विश्वास किसी काम का नहीं?

ru.L: Но хочешь ли ты знать, пустой человек, что вера без дел праздна?
ru.B: Хочешь, чтобы тебе показали, пустая ты голова, что вера без дел бездельна?
ru.R: Глупый человек! Хочешь, я покажу тебе, что вера без дел ни на что не годна?

decisions.choice: empty person: senseless, without substance
decisions.reason: κενέ means empty. The one who holds an empty faith is himself empty-headed. James addresses the objector of verse 18 directly, as Paul does in Romans 2:1 and 9:20.

decisions.choice: useless: idle, not working
decisions.reason: ἀργή means idle, unproductive. It is a play on words: the adjective is formed from the word for "work", so faith without works is a faith that does not work.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "useless"
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts, including the later majority, read νεκρά ("dead") here, the word of verses 17 and 26; copyists may have brought this verse into line with those. The SBLGNT reads ἀργή, which has strong early support and is the harder reading. From general knowledge; reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:person|man}}
decisions.reason: ἄνθρωπε addresses an imagined objector who could be anyone, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: does no work
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the wordplay between works and a faith that does not work.

decisions.choice: {{gender:persona vacía|hombre vacío}}
decisions.reason: Spanish has two ways to address ἄνθρωπε, "persona" and "hombre", so the gender setting carries over from the English; the adjective agrees with each option.

decisions.choice: haitendi chochote
decisions.reason: ἀργή (idle, not working) plays on ἔργων. "Matendo" and "haitendi" share the root -tenda, so Swahili keeps the wordplay, as the English Balanced does with "works ... no work".

decisions.choice: {{gender:personne vide|homme vide}} (L); {{gender:tête vide|homme vide}} (B); {{gender:Personne insensée|Homme insensé}} (R)
alternatives: ô homme vain, with no setting
decisions.reason: The word means a human being, man or woman. The adjective goes inside the span, since in the Readable default it must agree with "personne"; nothing else in the sentence refers back to the noun, so "personne" can be used here.

decisions.choice: "사람이여" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Greek word is "human being", used as a scornful address to anyone (meaning decision). Korean "사람" already covers men and women, and "남자여" would add a sense the Greek does not have.

decisions.choice: "người rỗng tuếch" (L, B), "Bạn" (R), with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" is a person of either sex, so the setting has nothing to offer here. "Rỗng tuếch" is empty, without substance (m1).

decisions.choice: não faz obra nenhuma
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the wordplay of m2 with Portuguese "obra", as the English keeps it with "work": a faith without works does no work.

decisions.choice: ሥራ ፈት (idle, literally "work-loosed") for useless
decisions.reason: The Greek word for useless is built on the word for work: faith without works does no work. Amharic "ሥራ ፈት" makes the same play on "ሥራ". Readable says plainly that it is good for nothing.

decisions.choice: "हे ... मनुष्य" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The word is anthropos, an imagined objector who could be anyone. "मनुष्य" already includes women and men in Hindi, so there is nothing for the English setting to change (style guide, section 7).

decisions.choice: "कोई काम नहीं करता" (B); "किसी काम का नहीं" (R)
decisions.reason: Hindi "काम" is both the works of the argument and "use", so Balanced and Readable can keep the wordplay of the Greek (faith without works does not work).

decisions.choice: человек; пустая ты голова (no gender span)
decisions.reason: The Greek here is anthropos, and Russian "человек" already means a person of either sex, so no span is needed where the English has one.

decisions.choice: бездельна
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the play on words, as the English does: faith without "дела" is "бездельна", idle (m2).

decisions.choice: "людино" with no gender span
decisions.reason: The Greek word is anthropos, which Ukrainian "людина" renders exactly and inclusively; the brief keeps gender spans out where Ukrainian is already inclusive.

decisions.choice: "人よ" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span with "男よ" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The English has a gender span on the address (person/man). Japanese "人" already addresses anyone, man or woman, and "男よ" would not be the traditional wording, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: "何の働きもしない" (B)
decisions.reason: m2: the adjective is a play on the word for work. Balanced lets "行い" and "働き" echo each other, as the English Balanced keeps works and does no work.
